description: Fix the open issues tracked in TODO/README.md, sourced from the upstream 101arrowz/fflate issue list. Ordered so that low-risk API additions land before the deep DEFLATE correctness bugs, since a stall in the loop halts everything after it.

userStories.title: Make FlateError a real exported class
userStories.description: As a consumer catching errors from fflate, I want `error instanceof FlateError` to work so that I can tell a corrupt archive apart from an unrelated failure like out-of-memory.
acceptanceCriteria: `FlateError` in src/index.ts becomes a class extending Error exported as a runtime value, replacing the current `export interface FlateError extends Error` at src/index.ts:221
The class keeps the `code: number` property and sets `name` to 'FlateError'; the message strings from the `ec` array at src/index.ts:200 are unchanged
`err()` (src/index.ts:228) constructs the class and still supports its `msg` override and `nt` no-throw argument
Add the class to the `bInflt` and `bDflt` payload arrays (src/index.ts:1096-1097) next to `err`, because `err` is stringified into the worker and would otherwise throw ReferenceError there
`keepNames` stays false in every esbuild config and no terser `compress` options are added (see CLAUDE.md Invariants)
A node test asserts that a sync API (e.g. inflateSync on corrupt input) throws a value satisfying `instanceof FlateError` with the expected `.code`
Existing `import type { FlateError }` style usages still compile
Typecheck passes
npm test passes (node and browser suites, plain and minified)
userStories.notes: FlateError is now a class in src/index.ts and is listed in bInflt. Deliberately NOT added to bDflt: that payload has no err and no deflate path constructs a FlateError. Async/worker errors are still plain Errors -- see US-002.

userStories.title: Preserve FlateError identity across the async and worker boundary

acceptanceCriteria: Errors passed to callbacks of the async APIs (e.g. `inflate`, `unzip`) and to `AsyncFlateStreamHandler` are `instanceof FlateError` with the correct `.code`
Errors crossing back from a worker are rehydrated on the main thread, since structured clone drops the class prototype
A node test covers at least one callback-style async API and one worker-backed streaming class
test/3-node-min.ts still passes against dist/node/index.min.js
Typecheck passes
npm test passes (node and browser suites, plain and minified)
userStories.notes: Rehydration lives in `rhyd`, called from `wrkr` (src/index.ts), the single choke point every async API and worker-backed stream goes through. Both spawners already preserve the numeric `code`; only the prototype was lost. Covered by test/5-async-error.ts against dist/node/index{,.min}.js.

userStories.title: Expose external file attributes and isDirectory on UnzipFileInfo
userStories.description: As someone reconstructing a directory tree from a ZIP, I want to know whether a central-directory entry is a directory so that I can tell a directory apart from an empty file without guessing from a trailing slash.
acceptanceCriteria: `UnzipFileInfo` (src/index.ts:3600) gains `attrs: number` (the external file attributes from the central directory record) and `isDirectory: boolean`
`isDirectory` is true when the MS-DOS directory bit (0x10) is set in the low byte, or the unix S_IFDIR bit is set in the high 16 bits, or the name ends with '/'

The filter object literals in BOTH `unzip` (near src/index.ts:3955) and `unzipSync` (near src/index.ts:4019) are updated in this same commit -- declaration emit fails otherwise (see CLAUDE.md Invariants)
Doc comments explain the attribute layout and which platforms populate it
A node test unzips a fixture archive containing a directory entry, an empty file, and a normal file, and asserts isDirectory for each
Typecheck passes
npm test passes (node and browser suites, plain and minified)

Local file headers carry no external attributes, so the streaming value is derived from the trailing '/' convention; the doc comment states this limitation explicitly and points at UnzipFileInfo.attrs for the reliable signal

userStories.notes: Derived from the trailing '/' convention via isdir(0, fn) -- local file headers have no external attributes field. Covered by the browser test `Unzip streaming isDirectory` in test/browser/zip.ts.

userStories.title: Expose the raw filename bytes on UnzipFileInfo
userStories.description: As someone opening archives whose filenames are cp866 or another non-UTF-8 encoding, I want the undecoded name bytes so that I can decode them myself with the right TextDecoder.
acceptanceCriteria: `UnzipFileInfo` gains `rawName: Uint8Array` (the filename bytes exactly as stored) and `nameIsUTF8: boolean` (bit 11 of the general purpose bit flag)
`name` keeps its current decoding behavior -- this is additive only
The filter object literals in BOTH `unzip` and `unzipSync` are updated in this same commit, for the same declaration-emit reason as US-003
A node test builds an archive with a non-UTF-8 filename, confirms `nameIsUTF8` is false, and confirms `new TextDecoder('cp866').decode(info.rawName)` yields the expected string

npm test passes (node and browser suites, plain and minified)
userStories.notes: `zh` now also returns the raw filename subarray and bit 11 of the general purpose bit flag; both filter literals pass them through as `rawName` / `nameIsUTF8`. `rawName` is a VIEW onto the caller's buffer, not a copy, to avoid an allocation per central directory entry. Covered by test/7-unzip-rawname.ts.

userStories.title: Stop emitting zero-length non-final chunks from streaming decompression
userStories.description: As a consumer of the streaming `Gunzip`/`Inflate` callbacks, I want no empty intermediate chunks so that the 0.8.3 sync-flush work does not change the emission pattern that downstream code relied on.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce TODO/callback.md first: gzip 'hello world', push it through `new Gunzip(cb)` with final=true, and observe the current [11/false, 0/false, 0/true] sequence
After the fix, a zero-length chunk is never emitted with `final: false`
Exactly one callback still fires with `final: true`, so end-of-stream is never lost even when the last chunk is empty
The behavior is consistent across `Inflate`, `Gunzip`, `Unzlib`, and `Decompress`
Sync-flush boundaries still work: a `flush()` that produces real bytes still emits them
Regression tests cover the callback.md repro and the flush-still-works case
Typecheck passes
npm test passes (node and browser suites, plain and minified)
userStories.notes: From TODO/callback.md. Fixed in the shared `Inflate.c`, which Gunzip/Unzlib call through and Decompress delegates to. Gunzip now emits [data/false, empty/true] rather than a single [data/true]: collapsing to one callback would require buffering the last member across the concatenated-member probe. Covered by test/8-stream-chunks.ts.

userStories.title: Document the streaming callback emission contract

CHANGELOG.md records the 0.8.3 emission change and the US-008 fix
No em dashes and no arrow characters, per the docs conventions
Do NOT run `npm run build-docs`

userStories.title: Diagnose the streaming Deflate invalid distance bug
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a written root cause for streaming `Deflate` emitting out-of-window back-references so that the fix session starts from a diagnosis instead of a symptom.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce TODO/streaming.md using the 234-byte base64 EMF prefix in that file, from a real .mjs or .cjs file rather than `node --input-type=module -e`

Confirm the reported shape: `deflateSync` and callback `deflate()` are byte-identical and valid, streaming `Deflate` is the same length but different bytes and rejected by both fflate's `inflateSync` and node's `zlib.inflateRawSync` with an invalid-distance error
Identify where the divergence begins and why the streaming path allows a distance larger than the bytes fed so far, e.g. window base or hash-chain bookkeeping that `deflateSync` gets right
Write specs/2026-08-08-streaming-deflate-invalid-distance.md naming the responsible function and line range in src/index.ts and describing the mechanism

No source or test changes in this story

userStories.notes: From TODO/streaming.md. Investigation only; no source or test changes. Root cause written up in specs/2026-08-08-streaming-deflate-invalid-distance.md: dflt's maxd bound (src/index.ts:741) uses the scratch-buffer index i, which is 32768 too large while dfltInit's reserved lookback region is still zero-filled. No overlap with US-010.

userStories.title: Fix streaming Deflate so it never emits an out-of-window distance
userStories.description: As a user streaming compression through `Deflate` or `ZipDeflate`, I want valid DEFLATE output so that off-the-shelf inflaters can read it.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement the fix identified in specs/2026-08-08-streaming-deflate-invalid-distance.md
A regression test runs the 234-byte EMF prefix through streaming `Deflate` and asserts both fflate's `inflateSync` and node's `zlib.inflateRawSync` recover the exact input
The test covers levels 1, 3, 6, and 9 and at least two chunk shapes, e.g. one push and 1-byte pushes, since TODO/streaming.md reports the bug is independent of both
A `ZipDeflate` case is covered too, since that wrapper is where the bug was originally found
Existing deflateSync output is byte-for-byte unchanged, verified against the existing test/1-size expectations
Typecheck passes
npm test passes (node and browser suites, plain and minified)
userStories.notes: Fixed per specs/2026-08-08-streaming-deflate-invalid-distance.md: DeflateState gained a `b` base index, dflt bounds maxd by `i - (st.b || 0)`, dfltInit seeds it to 32768 (or to the dictionary start), and Deflate.push resets it to 0 after the wrap copy. Regression guard is test/10-stream-window.ts.
